cards.name: Color Halftone
cards.summary: Simulates an enlarged halftone screen: each colour channel is cut into a grid of cells and every cell is replaced by a circle whose size follows that channel's brightness, with the grid of each channel rotated to its own screen angle. The photo turns into overlapping coloured dots with a rosette pattern, the classic pop-art / comic-print / newspaper look.
use_for: pop-art or comic-book treatment of a portrait or press photo for a poster or thumbnail
a retro newsprint / screen-printed texture on a background image behind a headline
a dotted overlay layer (set to Multiply, Overlay or Screen) that adds print texture without replacing the photo
big-dot graphic backgrounds for social cards and event banners
avoid: expecting black ink dots on white straight from an RGB file: in RGB the dots are red, green and blue light over dark gaps; convert to CMYK (Image > Mode) for ink-style CMYK dots, or, for a single-colour dot screen, use Grayscale mode (only Channel 1 is used) or a desaturated copy with all channel angles set to the same value (at the default 108/162/90 the red, green and blue grids sit at different angles, so a desaturated RGB copy still breaks into coloured dots)
faces at a large Radius: eyes and mouth dissolve into dots; keep faces on a masked unfiltered layer or use a smaller Radius
real print screening: this is a visual effect baked into the pixels, not a printer's halftone; send continuous-tone files to print
a missing key in a script: the harvest shows Photoshop reuses this filter's last-used value for an omitted key, so always send radius and all four angles

params.name: Radius
params.does: maximum dot radius in pixels (the dialog's Max. Radius); sets the size of the halftone cells, bigger = coarser, more graphic dots
params.typical: 4-10 px for a fine print texture, 15-40 px for bold pop-art dots on a 1920 px image

params.name: Channel 1
params.does: screen angle in degrees for the first channel (red in RGB, cyan in CMYK, the only channel used in Grayscale)
params.typical: 108 (Photoshop's default) in RGB; 15 for cyan in CMYK

params.name: Channel 2
params.does: screen angle in degrees for the second channel (green in RGB, magenta in CMYK)
params.typical: 162 (default) in RGB; 75 for magenta in CMYK

params.name: Channel 3
params.does: screen angle in degrees for the third channel (blue in RGB, yellow in CMYK)
params.typical: 90 (default) in RGB; 0 for yellow in CMYK

params.name: Channel 4
params.does: screen angle in degrees for the fourth channel (black in CMYK); not used by RGB or Grayscale images

pairs_with: Gaussian Blur or Median before it (smoother tones give cleaner, rounder dots)
Image > Mode > CMYK Color before it (ink-style CMYK rosette)
a duplicate layer in Multiply or Overlay with a layer mask (dot texture over the original photo)
Hue/Saturation or Vibrance afterwards (punchier pop-art colour)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("radius"), 20); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("angle1"), 108); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("angle2"), 162); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("angle3"), 90); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("angle4"), 45); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("colorHalftone"), d, DialogModes.NO);  // radius clamps to 4-127 px (harvest probe)
cards.non_destructive: no on a plain pixel layer (it rewrites the pixels); applied to a Smart Object it becomes an editable Smart Filter (general Photoshop behaviour, not probed by the harvest)
cards.cost: light-medium: 376 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer; time grows with image size

review.changes: avoid: 'work on a desaturated copy for a single-colour dot screen' was wrong with the card's own default angles (each RGB channel is screened on its own rotated grid, so identical grey channels still give offset coloured dots); now says Grayscale mode (Channel 1 only) or a desaturated copy with all angles equal. Rest checked against the batch (keys radius/angle1-4, int type, 4-127 clamp, defaults 108/162/90/45, demo in range, event colorHalftone, AI ClrH + CDR Halftone exist) and unchanged.

verified.note: The whole frame is enlarged overlapping CMY-style dots on rotated grids with a rosette pattern, saturated pure colours, the pop-art halftone look.

cards.name: Crystallize
cards.summary: Clumps pixels into irregular polygonal cells (like crystals or a Voronoi pattern) and fills each cell with one solid colour taken from the image under it. The image becomes a faceted, shattered-glass mosaic with no outlines between cells; Cell Size sets how big the shards are.
use_for: an abstract faceted background from a photo for a poster, title card or slide
a stylised shattered-glass / geometric treatment of a portrait for a thumbnail
obscuring a busy background (crowd, venue) while keeping its colours and composition
a colour-block base layer to trace or to combine with edge filters for a low-poly-like look
avoid: text, logos and thin lines: they break into shards and become unreadable; keep them on separate layers above
censoring a face or plate: irregular shards read as a decorative effect and small cells leave features recognisable; use Mosaic with a big Cell Size, or a solid filled box for anything sensitive
a leaded stained-glass look with dark borders between cells: Crystallize has no outlines; use Stained Glass (Filter Gallery) for that
a missing key in a script: the harvest shows Photoshop reuses this filter's last-used Cell Size when the key is omitted

params.name: Cell Size
params.does: average size of each crystal cell in pixels; bigger = fewer, larger flat-colour shards and more abstraction
params.typical: 8-20 for a textured look that keeps the subject, 30-80 for a bold abstract background on a 1920 px image

pairs_with: Find Edges or Poster Edges on a copy (draws outlines around the cells)
Gaussian Blur on a copy blended back (softer frosted-glass look)
Layer mask (keeps the subject sharp while the background crystallises)
Hue/Saturation or Gradient Map afterwards (recolours the facets for a brand palette)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("cellSize"), 40); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("crystallize"), d, DialogModes.NO);  // cellSize clamps to 3-300 (harvest probe)
cards.non_destructive: no on a plain pixel layer; on a Smart Object it is kept as an editable Smart Filter (general Photoshop behaviour, not probed by the harvest)
cards.cost: medium: 431 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer, the slowest filter in this batch

review.changes: summary: dropped the unverified claim that each cell's colour is averaged (docs and harvest only say pixels clump into one solid colour); avoid: the censoring bullet said 'large cells keep colours and shapes readable', which contradicts what large cells do, rewritten. cellSize int 3-300, demo 40, event crystallize, AI Crst + CDR Creative/Crystalize checked and unchanged.

verified.note: Irregular polygonal single-colour cells over everything, no outlines; the strip and type break into shard edges.

cards.name: Facet
cards.summary: One-step filter with no settings that clusters pixels of similar colour into small blocks of like-coloured pixels, smoothing out fine detail and grain so a photo starts to look hand-painted. A single pass is subtle on a large image (especially an already soft frame); designers usually run it several times in a row.
use_for: a light hand-painted / painterly base before Oil Paint, Poster Edges or Cutout
breaking up scanner or video-compression grain into small flat-colour patches
a subtle illustrative texture on a background photo behind text
avoid: expecting a strong, obvious effect from one pass on a 1920 px image: the change is small and easy to miss (the gallery sample may look nearly unchanged); repeat it several times or use Crystallize, Cutout or Oil Paint for a bold look
needing control: it has no settings at all; for adjustable smoothing use Median, Surface Blur or Oil Paint
sharp text and hairlines: edges get slightly blotchy; keep type on its own layer
pairs_with: Facet again (repeat 2-5 times for a stronger effect)
Oil Paint or Poster Edges (finishes the painted look)
Smart Sharpen afterwards (restores edge definition)
Median (a stronger, adjustable version of the same clean-up)
cards.scripting: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("facet"), new ActionDescriptor(), DialogModes.NO);  // no parameters; loop the call to repeat it
cards.non_destructive: no on a plain pixel layer; on a Smart Object it is kept as a Smart Filter (general Photoshop behaviour, not probed by the harvest)
cards.cost: light: 141 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer

review.changes: none: no params in the batch so no demo_settings; parameterless facet event call, status/scriptable and 141 ms cost match; the subtle-on-a-soft-plate warning is in avoid; no AI Pixelate or CDR item does the same job, so equivalents stay empty.

verified.note: Subtle as the card says: on the soft plate one pass shifts the photo by about 1 level on average (7 % of pixels over 4 levels), seen at 2x zoom as slightly firmer, blotchier edges (radial lines, fine detail); no 1:1 crop was made for it.

cards.name: Fragment
cards.summary: One-step filter with no settings that makes four copies of the pixels, offsets them a few pixels from each other and averages them, so every edge appears quadrupled. The result looks like a shaken camera or double vision: a soft, ghosted, jittery blur rather than a smooth one.
use_for: a dazed / dizzy / earthquake or shaken-camera feel on a still for a reel thumbnail or meme
a quick ghosted-edges glitch on a background photo behind text
suggesting impact or vibration on an object when combined with a mask
avoid: needing control over the amount or direction: there are no settings and the offset is a fixed few pixels, so on a large or already soft image (like a 1920 px video frame) it is subtle; repeat it, or use Motion Blur or duplicate layers offset by hand for a stronger, directed ghost
text and logos: type gets four overlapping outlines and reads as out of focus; keep it on a separate layer
a clean soft-focus look: use Gaussian Blur or Lens Blur instead
pairs_with: Fragment again (repeat to widen the ghosting)
Motion Blur (adds a direction to the shake)
RGB channel offset (Layer Style > Advanced Blending channel toggles on shifted copies) for a chromatic glitch
Layer mask (limits the shake to one subject)
cards.scripting: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("fragment"), new ActionDescriptor(), DialogModes.NO);  // no parameters; loop the call to repeat it
cards.non_destructive: no on a plain pixel layer; on a Smart Object it is kept as a Smart Filter (general Photoshop behaviour, not probed by the harvest)
cards.cost: light: 144 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer

review.changes: none: no params in the batch so no demo_settings; parameterless fragment event call, status/scriptable and 144 ms cost match; no AI or CDR counterpart found (CDR has only a Fragment brush bitmap preset), equivalents stay empty.

verified.note: Every edge is ghosted four times: the PGD type and hairlines read as doubled outlines and the photo looks shaken, as described.

cards.name: Mezzotint
cards.summary: Converts the image into a random pattern of dots, lines or strokes in which every channel is pushed to fully on or fully off, so a colour photo becomes a grainy pattern of pure saturated colours (red, green, blue, cyan, magenta, yellow, black, white) and a grayscale one becomes black and white. Tone survives only as the density of the pattern, giving a gritty engraving / photocopy / noise texture.
use_for: a gritty, high-energy grunge texture on a poster or album-style cover
a black-and-white engraved / photocopied look on a grayscale portrait (convert to grayscale first)
a streaky horizontal scan-line texture using a Lines or Strokes type, faded back over the photo
a noise overlay layer blended at low opacity for a print-grain feel
avoid: colour-accurate work: every channel is thresholded, so skin tones and brand colours turn into harsh primaries; convert to Grayscale mode first (Photoshop documents black-and-white areas for grayscale images) or blend the result back at low opacity
reproducible output: the pattern is random, so two runs never match exactly
faces and small type at full strength: they break up into noise; mask them or blend the effect
a regular dot screen: Mezzotint is random; use Color Halftone for an even dot grid

params.name: Type
params.does: shape of the random pattern: dots (fine to coarse), horizontal lines (short to long) or strokes (short to long)
params.typical: coarseDots or grainyDots for a grainy engraving look; longLines or longStrokes for streaky scan-line texture

pairs_with: Image > Mode > Grayscale before it (pure black-and-white mezzotint instead of primary-colour noise; a merely desaturated RGB layer is still screened channel by channel and is not guaranteed to stay neutral)
Gaussian Blur after it (softens the grain into a smoother texture)
Edit > Fade or reduced layer opacity / Overlay blend (keeps the photo, adds the grain)
Gradient Map (recolours the two-tone result into brand colours)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putEnumerated(stringIDToTypeID("mezzotintType"), stringIDToTypeID("mezzotintType"), stringIDToTypeID("coarseDots")); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("mezzotint"), d, DialogModes.NO);
cards.non_destructive: no on a plain pixel layer; on a Smart Object it is kept as an editable Smart Filter (general Photoshop behaviour, not probed by the harvest)
cards.cost: light: 298 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer

review.changes: avoid + pairs_with: recommended Desaturate / Black & White to get a black-and-white mezzotint, but the filter works per channel on an RGB layer; now points to Image > Mode > Grayscale, the mode the documented black-and-white result applies to. use_for: dropped 'rain' (the card's own Lines are horizontal). Enum key mezzotintType, 10 values + labels, demo coarseDots, AI Mztn checked and unchanged.

verified.note: Coarse random dots with every channel pushed to on or off: the photo becomes gritty pure yellow, red, white and black speckle, the blocks speckled in their primaries.

cards.name: Mosaic
cards.summary: Clumps pixels into a grid of square blocks and fills each block with one solid colour averaged from its pixels: the classic pixelation / censor effect. Cell Size sets the block width in pixels; large cells turn the image into a coarse grid of colour squares.
use_for: pixelating faces, licence plates or screens in a news or reel thumbnail (select the area first)
8-bit / pixel-art and retro-game styling of a photo or background
an abstract colour-grid background from a photo for a title card
a pixelate-to-reveal sequence of stills (several Cell Sizes stepping down)
avoid: redacting text or numbers with small cells: pixelation can be partly reversed or guessed; for sensitive information use a solid filled box
running it on the whole layer when only one face needs hiding: make a selection or work on a masked copy
crisp pixel art at a different output size: resizing afterwards blurs the block edges; resize with Nearest Neighbor or apply Mosaic at the final size
a missing key in a script: the harvest shows Photoshop reuses this filter's last-used Cell Size when the key is omitted

params.name: Cell Size
params.does: width and height of each square block in pixels; bigger = blockier, less recognisable
params.typical: 10-20 px for a light pixel texture, 30-60 px to fully hide a face on a 1920 px frame

pairs_with: Rectangular / Elliptical Marquee or Select Subject (pixelates only the face or plate)
Posterize or Indexed Color (limited palette for pixel-art styling)
Image Size with Nearest Neighbor resampling (keeps block edges hard when scaling)
Find Edges or a grid pattern overlay (adds tile borders between blocks)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putUnitDouble(stringIDToTypeID("cellSize"), stringIDToTypeID("pixelsUnit"), 32); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("mosaic"), d, DialogModes.NO);  // cellSize is a pixel unit value, clamps to 2-200 (harvest probe)
cards.non_destructive: no on a plain pixel layer; on a Smart Object it is kept as an editable Smart Filter (general Photoshop behaviour, not probed by the harvest)
cards.cost: very light: 77 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer, the fastest filter in this batch

review.changes: none: cellSize sent as pixelsUnit (declared_params), number 2-200, demo 32 in range and unmistakable on the plate, event mosaic; AI Create Object Mosaic... (ai_menu) and CDR Effects/Distort/Pixelate exist and do the same square-tile job (CDR Effects/Creative/Mosaic is a tile/grout look, correctly not used).

verified.note: Square pixel blocks of one averaged colour each (16 px in the 960 frame), the classic pixelation.

cards.name: Pointillize
cards.summary: Breaks the image into randomly placed round dots of colour, like a pointillist painting, and fills the gaps between the dots with the current background colour from the Tools panel. Cell Size sets the dot size; large cells give a confetti-like field of coloured dots on a plain canvas.
use_for: a pointillist / Seurat-style painterly treatment of a portrait or landscape for a poster
a festive confetti or bokeh-dot background made from a photo's colours
an abstract dotted texture layer blended over the original image
avoid: forgetting the background colour: the canvas between dots is the Tools panel background colour (not a filter setting), so set it first (white for paper, black for a night look) or the gaps may come out an unexpected colour
reproducible output: dot placement is random, so two runs never match exactly
an even, print-like dot grid: use Color Halftone instead
faces and type at large Cell Size: they dissolve into dots; mask them or keep them on separate layers

params.name: Cell Size
params.does: size of each colour dot in pixels; bigger = larger, sparser dots and more of the background colour showing
params.typical: 5-12 for a fine painterly texture, 20-40 for a bold confetti-dot look on a 1920 px image

pairs_with: Set the background colour first (white, black or a brand colour for the gaps)
Gaussian Blur afterwards (melts the dots into soft bokeh)
Reduced layer opacity over the original (dotted texture that keeps the subject readable)
Vibrance or Hue/Saturation (brighter dot colours)
cards.scripting: var d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(stringIDToTypeID("cellSize"), 24); executeAction(stringIDToTypeID("pointillize"), d, DialogModes.NO);  // cellSize clamps to 3-300 (harvest probe); the gap colour is app.backgroundColor, set it before the call
cards.non_destructive: no on a plain pixel layer; on a Smart Object it is kept as an editable Smart Filter (general Photoshop behaviour, not probed by the harvest)
cards.cost: light: 225 ms on the harvest's 480x270 test layer

review.changes: none: cellSize int 3-300, demo 24 in range, event pointillize, background-colour gap note matches Photoshop behaviour; AI Pntl and CDR Art Strokes/Pointillist exist.

verified.note: Random round colour dots with white gaps (the white background swatch) over the whole frame, confetti-like.
